name: the sessions of a node that is gone are adopted
comments: A persistent subscriber of node4 (thinker11) is away when node4 goes. While node4 is down, a
message is published for it on node1 (thinker10); then the subscriber comes back to node2. The
message must be there: the cluster adopted node4's session as soon as node4's lease ran out, and
kept collecting for it - not only when its client came back. On the default stand of stand.sh,
run from thinker10. xmq_sub prints what it receives with -v; the grep is the check.

timeline.command: xmq_sub -h thinker11 -p 2887 -u user -P User-Secret1 -V 5 -c -x 3600 -q 1 -i stand-orphan -t cluster/test/orphan -W 2 --quiet
xmq_pub -h thinker10 -p 2884 -u user -P User-Secret1 -V 5 -q 1 -i stand-orphan-publisher -t cluster/test/orphan -m published-while-away --quiet
xmq_sub -h thinker10 -p 2885 -u user -P User-Secret1 -V 5 -c -x 3600 -q 1 -i stand-orphan -t cluster/test/orphan -C 1 -W 10 -v | grep -q published-while-away
